mind_map.central_node: What a Bird Thought: The Expanding Mind, Cognitive Growth, and Humility Before Nature
plot_summary_nodes: Stanza 1 > The Eggshell Stage: The bird recalls living in a small, round, pale-blue eggshell, believing the entire world was small, round, and blue.
Stanza 2 > The Straw Nest Stage: After hatching into a cozy straw nest nestled by its mother, it assumes the world is made entirely of straw.
Stanza 3 > The Tree Branch Stage: Flying to a leafy branch, it sees green leaves all around, realizes its earlier blindness, and thinks the world is made of leaves.
Stanza 4 > The Infinite Sky Stage: Flying beyond the tree into the open blue sky, the bird realizes the world is an infinite mystery that no single creature can fully explain.
character_arc_nodes: The Little Bird (Developing Explorer): Developing creature whose worldview expands from eggshell isolation to infinite skyward wonder.
theme_and_moral_nodes: Primary Theme > Cognitive Growth & Expanding Horizons: As individuals grow and explore, their understanding of the world continuously expands.
Secondary Theme > Intellectual Humility: Recognizing that the universe is far vast and mysterious than our limited personal experiences.
Metaphorical Connection > Human Development: Parallels human childhood growth from family shelter to global awareness.
Moral Lesson > Open-Mindedness: Never assume your current limited perspective represents the whole truth.
key_grammar_nodes: Grammar Rule > Modals of Ability & Inability: Using 'Can', 'Cannot', and 'Could' (e.g., 'I could see leaves', 'I cannot tell—can you?').
Grammar Rule > Past Tense Narrative Verbs: Lived, thought, hatched, flew, saw.
Vocabulary > Nestled (settled snugly), Pale-blue (light blue color), Blind (unaware/narrow-minded), Beyond (further than).
Poetic Reflection & Closing Question: Ending with an open rhetorical question ('I cannot tell—can you?') to prompt reader contemplation.
